paper.title: Learning Probably Approximately Correct Maximin Strategies in Simulation-Based Games with Infinite Strategy Spaces

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-confidence maximin identification in two-player zero-sum SBGs with finite strategy spaces (GP prior)
unmapped: Arms are strategy profiles (x,y) in an n x m grid; goal is identifying the maximin profile argmax_x min_y u(x,y) (maximin action identification)
Utility u drawn from a GP(0,k) prior with k(pi,pi)=sigma^2<=1; learner knows the kernel and the Gaussian noise variance lambda
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the simulator is given a strategy profile $\boldsymbol{\pi}_t \in \Pi$ and returns an estimated utility $\tilde{u}_t \coloneqq u(\boldsymbol{\pi}_t) + e_t$, where $e_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \lambda)$ is i.i.d.~Gaussian noise.

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-budget maximin identification in two-player zero-sum SBGs with finite strategy spaces (GP prior)
unmapped: Arms are strategy profiles (x,y) in an n x m grid; goal is identifying the maximin profile (maximin action identification), fixed budget T
Utility u drawn from a GP(0,k) prior; Gaussian noise variance lambda
settings.definition_quote: An alternative is to consider the \emph{fixed-budget} case, where the maximum number of rounds $T$ is given in advance, and the goal is to minimize the probability $\delta$ that $\bar{x}$ is not an $\epsilon$-maximin strategy

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-confidence epsilon-maximin identification in SBGs with infinite strategy spaces (GP prior)
unmapped: Goal is identifying an epsilon-maximin strategy over X x Y with X,Y closed intervals in [0,1]
Learner knows the kernel smoothness constants a, b of Assumption 1 (used to set grid size K_eps)
settings.definition_quote: A \emph{two-player zero-sum game with infinite strategy spaces} is a tuple $\Gamma = (\X, \Y, u)$ ... we focus on the case in which $\X \subset [0,1]$ and $\Y \subset [0,1]$ are closed intervals.

symbols.H_star: H^*(u) = sum over profiles of c(pi), maximin hardness
symbols.lam_noise: variance lambda of the Gaussian simulator noise

conditions: u drawn from GP(0,k) with k(pi,pi)=sigma^2<=1
maximin value differs from second-best maximin value
tuning: b_t = 2 log(n m pi^2 t^2/(6 delta))

source.label: thm:fixed_confidence
source.quote: Using a generic nondecreasing exploration term $b_t > 0$, the M-GP-LUCB algorithm stops its execution after at most $T_\delta$ rounds, where: T_\delta \leq \inf \{t : 8 H^*(u) b_t \lambda - \frac{\lambda n m}{\sigma^2} < t \}. Specifically, letting $b_t := 2 \log ( \frac{n m \pi^2 t^2}{6 \delta} )$, the algorithm returns a maximin profile with confidence at least $1 - \delta$, and: T_\delta \leq 64 H^*(u) \lambda (...)

results.notes: Stopping time bound holds on the good event (prob >= 1-delta); returns exact maximin with prob >= 1-delta. Generic b_t bound (inf form) not separately recorded.

symbols.lam_noise: variance lambda of Gaussian simulator noise
symbols.H_2m: H_2 = max_i i Delta_(i)^{-2}, with Delta_(i) = |u(pi*) - u(pi^i)| sorted over all profiles

source.label: thm:fixed_budget
source.quote: Letting $T$ be the number of available rounds, the GP-SE algorithm returns a maximin strategy profile $\bpi^\ast$ with confidence at least $1 - \delta_T$, where: \delta_T \coloneqq 2 P (n + m - 2) e^{-\frac{T - P}{8 \lambda \overline{\log}(P) H_2}}, and $H_2 \coloneqq \max_{i} i \, \Delta_{(i)}^{-2}$.

symbols.H_star: H^*(u) maximin hardness of the discretized game
symbols.K_eps: grid size ceil(b/(2 epsilon) sqrt(log(4a/delta))) + 1 per player
symbols.a_k: constant a in kernel smoothness Assumption 1
symbols.b_k: constant b in kernel smoothness Assumption 1

conditions: u drawn from GP(0,k) satisfying kernel smoothness Assumption 1 with constants a,b
tuning: b_t = 2 log(n m pi^2 t^2/(3 delta))
grid with K >= K_eps equally spaced points per player

source.label: cor:cont_conf
source.quote: Assume that $u$ is drawn from a GP satisfying Assumption~\ref{ass:smooth}. Given $\epsilon > 0$ and $\delta \in (0,1)$, letting $b_t := 2 \log ( \frac{n m \pi^2 t^2}{3 \delta} )$, the M-GP-LUCB algorithm applied to $\Gamma(K)$ with $K$ at least $K_\epsilon$ returns a strategy profile ... such that $\mathbb{P} ( |u(\bpi^\ast) - u(\bar{x}, y^\ast(\bar{x}))| \leq \epsilon ) \geq 1- \delta$. Moreover, the algorithm stops its execution after at most: T_{\delta, \epsilon} \leq 64 H^*(u) \lambda [...]

results.notes: Epsilon-maximin with probability >= 1-delta; the stopping-time bound is stated as an upper bound on number of rounds.

bound.expression_latex: 4 K^2_\epsilon (K_\epsilon - 1) e^{-\frac{T - K^2_\epsilon}{8 \lambda \overline{\log}(K^2_\epsilon) H_2}} + 2 a e^{-\frac{b^2}{4 \epsilon^2 (K_\epsilon - 1)^2}}

symbols.H_2m: H_2 = max_i i Delta_(i)^{-2} over discretized profiles

conditions: u drawn from GP(0,k) satisfying kernel smoothness Assumption 1
tuning: grid with K >= K_eps equally spaced points per player

source.label: cor:cont_budget
source.quote: Given $\epsilon > 0$ and $\delta \in (0,1)$, letting $T$ be the number of available rounds, the GP-SE algorithm applied to $\Gamma(K)$ with $K$ at least $K_\epsilon$ returns a profile ... such that $\mathbb{P} ( |u(\bpi^\ast) - u(\bar{x}, y^\ast(\bar{x}))| > \epsilon ) < \delta_{T, \epsilon}$, where: \delta_{T,\epsilon} \coloneqq 4 K^2_\epsilon (K_\epsilon - 1) e^{...} + 2 a e^{-\frac{b^2}{4 \epsilon^2 (K_\epsilon - 1)^2}}.

results.notes: Probability of not returning an epsilon-maximin profile.
